question: Under the CRR, when is an obligor considered to be in default?
expected_answer: When either or both apply: (a) the institution considers the obligor unlikely to pay its credit obligations in full without recourse to actions such as realising security; (b) the obligor is more than 90 days past due on any material credit obligation to the institution, its parent or subsidiaries.
author: claude-draft
notes: Wording checked in consolidated text (2026-06-26 version).

question: Can a bank apply the definition of default at facility level instead of obligor level, and for which exposures?
expected_answer: Yes, but only for retail exposures: institutions may apply points (a) and (b) of Art. 178(1) at the level of an individual credit facility rather than the total obligations of a borrower.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in text. Alternatives accepted 2026-10-27 (retrieval review).

question: What are the maximum absolute and relative components of the materiality threshold for retail past-due credit obligations?
expected_answer: Absolute component: at most EUR 100 (or national-currency equivalent) for the sum of amounts past due; relative component: between 0% and 2.5% of total on-balance exposures to the obligor, set at 1% unless the competent authority justifies otherwise. Both must be exceeded for the obligation to be material. Non-retail absolute component is at most EUR 500.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: What is the minimum probation period before a defaulted exposure (not under distressed restructuring) can be reclassified as non-defaulted?
expected_answer: At least 3 months after the conditions of Art. 178(1)(b) and 178(3) cease to be met, taking into account the obligor's behaviour and financial situation during that period.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Alternatives accepted 2026-10-27 (retrieval review).

question: How long is the probation period for a defaulted exposure subject to distressed restructuring?
expected_answer: At least 1 year from the latest of: (a) extending the restructuring measures, (b) the exposure being classified as defaulted, (c) the end of the grace period in the restructuring arrangements. Reclassification also requires, among others, a material payment during that period, no past-due amounts and no remaining concerns about full repayment.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Alternatives accepted 2026-10-27 (retrieval review).

question: What diminished financial obligation threshold should trigger default for a distressed restructuring?
expected_answer: Institutions set a threshold for the diminished financial obligation (DO = (NPV0 - NPV1)/NPV0, discounted at the original effective interest rate) that should not be higher than 1%; above it the exposure is considered defaulted.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: When does the sale of credit obligations at a loss indicate unlikeliness to pay?
expected_answer: When the credit-related economic loss on the sale (L = (E - P)/E) is material; institutions set the materiality threshold, which should not be higher than 5%.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in text.

question: What PD input floors apply to retail exposures under CRR3?
expected_answer: 0.1% for QRRE revolvers and 0.05% for other retail exposures; the PD used is the higher of the grade/pool PD and the floor. PD of defaulted retail exposures is 100%.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in text.

question: What minimum length of historical observation period is required for PD estimation?
expected_answer: At least five years for at least one data source, for both non-retail (Art. 180(1)(h)) and retail (Art. 180(2)(e)) exposures.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: What LGD input floors apply to retail exposures under CRR3?
expected_answer: Unsecured: QRRE 50%, other retail 30%. Secured: retail secured by residential property 5%; other retail secured by financial collateral 0%, by receivables 10%, by residential or commercial immovable property 10%, by other physical collateral 15%.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: Into which categories must deficiencies be classified when quantifying the margin of conservatism (MoC)?
expected_answer: Category A: identified data and methodological deficiencies; Category B: relevant changes to underwriting standards, risk appetite, collection and recovery policies and other sources of additional uncertainty; Category C: the general estimation error.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: How does the CRR define a 'large corporate'?
expected_answer: A corporate undertaking with consolidated annual sales of more than EUR 500 million, or belonging to a group whose total consolidated annual sales exceed EUR 500 million.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in text.

question: Under the CRR3 standardised approach, what risk weight applies to the part of a residential mortgage exposure up to 55% of the property value?
expected_answer: 20% (loan-splitting approach), with the 55% reduced by more senior liens not held by the institution.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in text.

question: What output floor factor may institutions apply in 2026 under the transitional arrangements?
expected_answer: 55% for 1 January to 31 December 2026 (phase-in: 50% 2025, 55% 2026, 60% 2027, 65% 2028, 70% 2029; end state x = 72.5% under Art. 92(3)). A Member State may decide that the un-floored total risk exposure amount applies at solo level.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: A bank has A-IRB permission. Can it use its own LGD and CCF estimates for a corporate group with EUR 800 million consolidated sales?
expected_answer: No. The obligor is a large corporate (sales > EUR 500m), and under CRR3 exposures to large corporates (not in the specialised lending class) must use the supervisory LGD values of Art. 161(1) and SA-CCFs, i.e. F-IRB treatment.
author: claude-draft
notes: Art. 151(8)(c) checked in text. Needs definition lookup + scope rule.

question: In a jurisdiction where the competent authority set the retail materiality threshold at EUR 100 and 1%, a retail obligor owes EUR 120 past due, which is 3% of its exposure, for 95 days, then pays it off. Is it in default, and when can it return to non-default?
expected_answer: Yes: both the absolute (EUR 120 > EUR 100) and relative (3% > 1%) components are exceeded and the obligation has been past due more than 90 days, so it is in default. After repayment it can return to non-default only after a probation period of at least 3 months, considering the obligor's behaviour and financial situation.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: What does the regulatory framework require for downturn LGD, and what applies if no downturn can be observed in the bank's data?
expected_answer: Institutions must use LGD estimates appropriate for an economic downturn where more conservative than the long-run average (Art. 181(1)(b)). The RTS specifies how the downturn period is identified; its duration (Art. 4) is based on the most severe 12-month values of the economic indicators, and recital 14 states a downturn period should last at least 12 months. Where neither observed nor estimated downturn impact is available, the institution must include a strictly positive Category A MoC, and the final downturn LGD including MoC must be at least min(long-run average LGD + 15 percentage points, 105%).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Note: 105% bounds the floor (min of LRA+15pp and 105%).

question: A defaulted corporate loan is restructured with a 2% NPV loss. How should the bank classify it and when can it be cured?
expected_answer: A 2% NPV loss exceeds the maximum 1% diminished-financial-obligation threshold, so the restructuring is a distressed restructuring and the exposure is (or stays) defaulted. It can return to non-default only after at least 1 year from the latest of extending the restructuring measures, the default classification, or the end of any grace period, and only if the para. 73 conditions are met (e.g. a material payment, no past-due amounts, no concerns about full repayment).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: An A-IRB bank recognises financial collateral in its own LGD estimates for other retail exposures. Which CRR requirements and floors apply?
expected_answer: It must consider the dependence between the risk of the obligor and that of the funded credit protection or its provider (Art. 181(1)(c)), and treat currency mismatches between the obligation and the collateral conservatively (Art. 181(1)(d)). The LGD input floor for other retail exposures secured by financial collateral is 0% (Art. 164(4), Table 1), compared with 30% if unsecured.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Replaces the earlier guarantee question.

question: What back-testing must an IRB bank perform on PD estimates, and how are the results reported to the ECB?
expected_answer: Under Art. 185(b) the bank must regularly compare realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade and analyse deviations outside the expected range, and do the same for own LGD and CCF estimates. Per the ECB instructions of February 2019, significant institutions submit the results with their annual validation report, using the ECB templates; tests include discriminatory power (e.g. AUC). The answer should note the instructions predate CRR3.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Source is the Feb 2019 version; answer should state the date.

question: Which floors constrain the capital requirement of an IRB retail mortgage portfolio in 2026?
expected_answer: Input floors apply per exposure: PD at least 0.05% (retail other than QRRE revolvers) and LGD at least 5% for retail exposures secured by residential property. The output floor (factor 55% in 2026) applies to the institution's total risk exposure amount, not to the portfolio alone, comparing it with the standardised approach (where mortgages use 20% up to 55% of property value); a Member State may exempt the solo level.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: Which CRR3 provision changed the PD input floor for IRB corporate exposures, and to what value?
expected_answer: Article 1, point (86) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1623 replaced CRR Art. 160(1), setting a PD input floor of 0.05% for corporate exposures (and inserting a separate Art. 160(1a) for regional governments, local authorities and public sector entities).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Old CRR2 value not in corpus, so the question avoids it.

question: What changed in the June 2026 release of the ECB guide to internal models?
expected_answer: Release 4.1 (26 June 2026) removed all content related to CCF estimation; release 4.0 (28 July 2025) had updated the guide for regulatory changes (CRR3).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in the release table.

question: Does the ECB guide to internal models apply to a less significant institution supervised by its national competent authority?
expected_answer: The guide explains how the ECB understands and applies the CRR when it grants internal-model permissions, i.e. for the institutions it supervises directly (significant institutions). It is not law, does not overrule EU or national law, and does not address LSIs. For an LSI the binding requirements remain the CRR, RTS and EBA guidelines as applied by its national competent authority; any use of the guide by NCAs is outside this corpus.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: How is the sensitivities-based method for market risk own funds requirements calculated under FRTB?
expected_answer: Abstain: market risk (FRTB) is outside the credit risk corpus.
author: claude-draft
notes: Note the CRR is in the corpus, so the system must recognise the topic, not just the source.

question: What is the required stable funding factor for residential mortgages under the NSFR?
expected_answer: Abstain: liquidity (NSFR) is outside the credit risk corpus.
author: claude-draft
notes: Tempting: NSFR text is in the full CRR file but outside the MVP scope.

question: What customer due diligence must a bank perform when onboarding a corporate client under the AML rules?
expected_answer: Abstain: anti-money-laundering requirements are outside the corpus.
author: claude-draft
